notes: The change adds a deprecated compatibility layer (legacy.mjs) as the class's last layer: 14 new public methods, and overrides of accountUsesSet, accountUses, accountUsesOf and accountFor that accept an old form and (for the last three) hand back more. Every addition to an answer is an optional member, which the method counts as hands back differently. The tool may also list private _legacy* members as new entries (uncommented). Because aiAccountsOf's answer is the class instance, written in full, any change to the class's members reads as aiAccountsOf handing back differently and tells every user of aiAccountsOf; that is most of the 26 users and is the largest source of notices I expect here. If the tool compares the class entry's members one by one rather than the instance as a whole, those notices go to the four changed methods' users only.

The change is inside aiAccountsOps' handlers: a member's own act (aiownadd, aimineuse, aimycheckset, aipersonalchoose, aiorderset with owner member) now takes a stamp already written member:<id> as the owner as it stands, instead of prefixing it again. No kind changes; my comments never stated the form of the stamp `by` (only that it is the control plane's), so no comment needed to change. Had the first comments bound `by` to a bare member id, this would read as accepts more on those ops (tells nobody). If the tool notices the code change without a listing change, it should tell nobody.

Inside the deprecated subscriptionTokenHold: the acts it makes on the member's behalf (accountSet, accountSwitch) now pass `by` as member:<id> instead of the bare id, so the disclosure registered under member:<id> is found. What it accepts and hands back is unchanged (it could already answer DISCLOSURE_DUE as a Refusal). No comment needed to change.

entries.why: weight's kind gained 'reversible' and 'terminal' and lost 'caller-owned' (no row carries it now)
each row is a DeclaredOp, whose weight kind changed

notes: The change regrades the declared ops (DECLARED_OPS' weight per row, to op-grades R57's grades). The kind written for a row (DeclaredOp, built by D) carries the set of weights, not each row's own, so the listing shows only the set changing; which op moved from which weight to which is content the kinds do not hold. Users that read DECLARED_OPS (store-assembly's declarations, op-declarations, op-grades through them) are the ones to tell. If the tool widens literal values of a constant only when no comment states its kind, it will not see the per-row values at all.
